review.rationale: The supplied Gold is an appropriate independent expectation for this intentionally pending planning case. It preserves REQ-001, AC-001 through AC-003, repository identity and base commit, and the paired-case reference. DEC-001 materially determines exception propagation and abort-versus-throw precedence; the conditional acceptance language does not resolve it. Gold therefore correctly requires blocked readiness with requirement-decision-pending on DEC-001 and evidence through repository, requirements, and decisions, without assignable task or assignment expectations. The supplied runtime policy explicitly places this decision gate before Scenario Coverage, so the empty team catalog and missing later-stage reviewer do not invalidate this expected stopping boundary. Source evidence and package exports support index.js and the separately maintained index.d.ts as implementation owners, with test.js and index.test-d.ts serving runtime and type verification respectively; package.json specifies xo && ava && tsd. The visible delay calculation supports the specified decreasing-backoff and zero-delay expectations, and the pre-delay cancellation boundary makes the hook-induced abort cases coherent. The proposed Gold and preview release fingerprints match across repository, source, team, decision input, prompts, model, sampling, budgets, and metric policy. I accept those fingerprints as Service-calculated bindings, not independently recomputed hashes. The truncated runtime-test excerpt does not prevent evaluating this decision-stage expectation. No candidate, execution result, human Decision, or human attestation was assumed; any fixed hypothetical C input would not resolve DEC-001 for this case.
